headline: 69 workers rescued as fire hits Gazipur garment factory
summary: Firefighters brought the blaze at Matrix Garments under control after nearly four hours, rescuing dozens of trapped workers from the rooftop.
details: A massive fire broke out at the seven-story Matrix Garments factory in the Degerchala area of Gazipur City Corporation on Saturday afternoon.
The blaze started around 2:45 PM, reportedly originating from a warehouse on the third floor, leading to widespread panic among the workers.
Many workers rushed to the rooftop to escape the smoke and flames, while others scrambled to exit the building through the lower floors.
Nine fire service units, including two from the Bhogra Modern Fire Station, worked for nearly four hours to bring the fire under control.
During the operation, firefighters successfully rescued 69 workers who had become trapped on the roof of the building.
While a large amount of goods were destroyed in the fire, no casualties or injuries have been reported so far.
The exact cause of the fire and the total extent of the financial loss are yet to be determined.
caption:
69 workers were trapped on the roof of a seven-story garment factory in Gazipur as a massive fire broke out.

A massive fire broke out at the seven-story Matrix Garments factory in the Degerchala area of Gazipur City Corporation on Saturday afternoon.

The blaze started around 2:45 PM, reportedly originating from a warehouse on the third floor, leading to widespread panic among the workers.

Many workers rushed to the rooftop to escape the smoke and flames, while others scrambled to exit the building through the lower floors.

Nine fire service units, including two from the Bhogra Modern Fire Station, worked for nearly four hours to bring the fire under control.

During the operation, firefighters successfully rescued 69 workers who had become trapped on the roof of the building.

While a large amount of goods were destroyed in the fire, no casualties or injuries have been reported so far.

The exact cause of the fire and the total extent of the financial loss are yet to be determined.

headline_marked: Ex-lawmaker [[Akhtaruzzaman on one-day remand]] for airport disorder
headline: Ex-lawmaker Akhtaruzzaman on one-day remand for airport disorder
summary: Former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman was placed on remand after allegedly assaulting a security official and threatening the airport executive director at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: A Dhaka court has placed former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman on a one-day remand. He is facing charges of assaulting an on-duty security official, obstructing government work, and creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

The incident occurred on Thursday morning near the baggage belt area. Passengers arriving from Madinah on a Biman flight faced delays in receiving luggage due to heavy pressure and a shortage of trolleys, leading to agitation among passengers.

According to the case statement, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly hurled abuse at the airport Executive Director, Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, and threatened him, saying, "I will beat you, I will grab you by the neck, and throw you out."

The situation escalated when security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked people accompanying the lawmaker to stop recording videos in a restricted Key Point Installation area. Akhtaruzzaman allegedly verbally abused and physically assaulted him.
It was further alleged that the lawmaker threw bottles of Zamzam water off trolleys, damaging them and behaving rudely towards a Biman representative.
Detectives arrested him from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area. He joined Jamaat-e-Islami in December last year after being expelled from the BNP.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Alberuni Mir passed the order for remand after police requested a five-day remand prayer.
